text: Fill in the missing terms about lipid classification and fatty acid chemistry.
questions: In Bloor's classification, phospholipids and glycolipids are *compound:Simple lipids have only fatty acid + alcohol; what class carries an additional group?* lipids because they carry an extra group — phosphate or carbohydrate — beyond the fatty acid and alcohol.

The products of lipid hydrolysis — fatty acids, glycerol, cholesterol and fat-soluble vitamins — are grouped as *derived:The third class in Bloor's scheme — hydrolysis products and related molecules.* lipids in Bloor's classification.

In omega numbering the first double bond is counted from the *methyl:Omega numbering counts from which end of the fatty acid chain?* end, so linoleic acid is omega-6 and alpha-linolenic acid is omega-3.

Linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid are *essential:What do we call nutrients the body cannot synthesise and must obtain from food?* fatty acids because human desaturases cannot place a double bond beyond carbon 9.
In delta numbering the double bond position is counted from the *carboxyl:Delta numbering counts from which functional group at the start of the chain?* end, so oleic acid is Δ9.

overallFeedback.feedback: Bloor's three classes — simple (fatty acid + alcohol esters), compound (carry an extra phosphate or sugar group), and derived (hydrolysis products) — organise lipids by what they yield on hydrolysis. Delta numbering counts from the carboxyl end (Δ9 for oleic acid) while omega numbering counts from the methyl end (ω-6 for linoleic, ω-3 for alpha-linolenic); linoleic and alpha-linolenic are essential because human desaturases cannot act beyond Δ9.
